message:
test(host): execute the branch for a helper that will not die

Test 1, build 1. Built, not run -- same reason as df07b76.

The lingering branch could not be reached. TerminateProcess does not fail for a process this one
started, so the confirmation always succeeded, the branch never ran, and deleting it would have
broken no test. Writing UNEXERCISED on it was honest and was not coverage.

This target links host_thumbnail_kill_fault.cpp in place of host_thumbnail_kill.cpp. The one OS
call at the teardown boundary reports failure and terminates nothing; every other line is the
product. The helper really does stay alive, the handles really are held, the next request really is
refused -- and then the test kills the helper itself and checks the host notices.

What it asserts: the first capture times out and reports the kill unconfirmed; the next request
comes back as thumb_helper_lingering, as Canceled so the window is not charged for a refusal that
is ours, in microseconds rather than a deadline, and WITHOUT starting a second helper -- one alive
after two requests is the bound the whole design rests on. It prints the stage breakdown for the
lingering path, which is the row the V9 table was missing.

What it starts: one copy of itself, named GNLinkCapture.exe in a scratch directory, which sleeps.
No host, no sockets, no screen capture, no firewall prompt. It is the lightest thing in this suite
and it is still a process the user did not ask for, so it waits with the rest.

The substitution is link-time, so nothing of it reaches the shipping binaries, and
shipped_helper_gate_test reads both of them to say so. That gate was itself worthless when first
written -- the marker was unreferenced and the linker dropped it -- which is why it is checked by
mutation now.
